dedupe_keys.name: shift a dem based spatial heterogeneity improved mapping of global geomorphic floodplains

description: Peking University publishes SHIFT, a global map of geomorphic floodplains derived from MERIT-Hydro terrain and a floodplain-hydraulic-geometry threshold. Spatially varying scaling parameters are estimated for level-three basins. Zenodo provides 90 m and 1 km GeoTIFFs plus a parameter Shapefile, openly and free under CC-BY-4.0. The original 90 m layer includes lakes and reservoirs; the 1 km layer marks these separately. Values identify floodplain, non-floodplain and missing areas, using WGS84 coordinates. The product is a static geomorphic delineation, not a time series or a flood map at a specified return period. That limitation prevents interpreting each floodplain pixel as a predicted inundation event. SHIFT could help screen infrastructure locations or define domains for more detailed flood simulations. It complements hydrodynamic hazard maps with a terrain-based floodplain boundary and published regional parameters. No raster or algorithm was run.
name: SHIFT: A DEM-Based Spatial Heterogeneity Improved Mapping of Global Geomorphic Floodplains
